codeReview.summary: Review failed. The fix adds useful host observability hooks, but the revised VAL-CROSS-010 tests still do not prove queued reload execution, rebuild/presentation counts, or real dependency filtering against the ComponentHost dependency set, so the original blocking evidence gap remains.

issues.description: The same-turn coalescing proof still stops at scheduling. `testObservedObjectReloadsCoalesceWithinOneTurn` leaves the prior placeholder `XCTAssertTrue(true)` in place and never waits for the deferred main-actor task or asserts `executedReloadCount`, `onReloadContentCompleted`, or a new render/present count, so a regression where the queued reload never executes would still pass. `testObservedObjectCoalescingByDependencyRelevance` has the same gap: it records `reloadCompletedCount` but never asserts it and explicitly notes that the scheduled task may not have executed.

The dependency-filtering claim is still unproven. `testUnrelatedObservedObjectChangesDoNotTriggerReload` only shows that an object with no registered observer does not notify the host. It does not exercise the filtering branch in `scheduleObservedObjectReload` because manual `host.observe(...)` only installs tokens, while `componentHost.observedObjects` is populated during `reloadContent` in `Sources/WinSwiftUI/App.swift:315-326`; with `content: []`, that set stays empty and the `dependsOnChangedObject` check at `Sources/WinSwiftUI/App.swift:403-409` never rejects a scheduled reload. The fix therefore still lacks validator-visible evidence that a changed-but-non-dependent observed object is filtered out by the current component tree.

summary: Fail: although the fix adds observability seams, it still does not prove deferred reload execution or true dependency filtering, so VAL-CROSS-010 remains non-visible to scrutiny.
